meanings.note: Aider quelqu'un, no preposition. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to help'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aidé').
Jeudi, alors. Invariable French adverb meaning 'then'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Invariable French adverb meaning 'then'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Feminine: assistante. Masculine noun ('le assistant', plural 'les assistants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'assistant'.

examples.text: Vous êtes l'assistante de Mathias Barneville?

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
C'est bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: À bientôt = see you soon. Invariable French adverb meaning 'soon'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
the standard greeting until evening
determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Comparison: comme un rêve. Core French preposition meaning 'like', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Conjunction. Core French preposition meaning 'like', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: Donner quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to give'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'donné').

examples.text: Fais du vélo! Ça donne des forces.
examples.trans: Ride a bike! It gives you energy.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: very frequent in speech; the t of fait is pronounced

examples.text: Bonjour. En fait, vous et lui...

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: faire la surprise à = to surprise
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: ça fait trois semaines que = it's been three weeks since
meanings.note: With time. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

meanings.note: c'est gentil = that's kind (of you)

examples.text: C'est gentil, mais je suis bien ici.
examples.trans: That's kind, but I'm fine here.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'here'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Indirect object. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'to him'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Stressed form: avec lui. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'to him'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
être là = to be here, to be present
Invariable French adverb meaning 'there'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!. French conjunction meaning 'but', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
faire du mal à quelqu'un = to hurt someone
J'ai mal = it hurts. Masculine noun ('le mal', plural 'les maux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'harm'.
Ça va mal. Masculine noun ('le mal', plural 'les maux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'harm'.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas te faire de mal.
examples.trans: I don't want to hurt you.

meanings.note: Être marié(e) avec quelqu'un. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'married'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Du matin = a.m., in the morning. Masculine noun ('le matin', plural 'les matins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'morning'.

examples.text: Je peux t'appeler à quatre heures du matin? Tu travailles le dimanche?
examples.trans: Can I call you at four in the morning? Do you work on Sundays?

meanings.note: Before the verb; m' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
ma before a feminine noun, mon before a vowel

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?
Tag at the end of a question. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: before the noun; nouvel before a vowel
Un nouveau caprice. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'new'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Parce qu' before a vowel. French conjunction meaning 'because', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Parce que tu ne peux pas.
Parce que tu ne peux pas. C'est ma vie!
examples.trans: Because you can't. It's my life!

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: c'est pas possible! = I can't believe it!
Masculine: un poste. Masculine noun ('le poste', plural 'les postes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'job'.
feminine: la poste, a different word

examples.text: Je cherche un poste dans le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm looking for a job in film.

examples.text: Si tu veux, je peux t'aider à trouver un poste dans le cinéma.
examples.trans: If you want, I can help you find a job in film.

meanings.note: in questions and after verbs like comprendre, savoir

examples.text: Pourquoi est-ce que tu ne m'as rien dit hier?
examples.trans: Why didn't you tell me anything yesterday?

examples.text: Je comprends enfin pourquoi elle a refusé ce film.
examples.trans: I finally understand why she turned down that film.

meanings.note: + infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'can, to be able to'.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez
starts a question: qu'est-ce que tu fais? = what are you doing?

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais à Paris?
examples.trans: What are you doing in Paris?

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais à Paris? Tu es en vacances?
examples.trans: What are you doing in Paris? Are you on holiday?

meanings.note: Joins two parts: dis-lui que. French conjunction meaning 'that', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Relative: tout ce que. French conjunction meaning 'that', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
With ne: ne... que. French conjunction meaning 'that', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Ça fait trois semaines que. French conjunction meaning 'that', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: with ne: je ne promets rien; rien n'est signé

examples.text: Rien n'est signé. On attend l'appel.
examples.trans: Nothing is signed. We're waiting for the call.

meanings.note: bien / mal réagir = to react well / badly

examples.text: Écoute, j'ai mal réagi ce matin.
examples.trans: Listen, I reacted badly this morning.

meanings.note: s'attendre à + noun or infinitive: je ne m'attendais pas à te voir

examples.text: Je ne m'attendais pas à ça.
Je ne m'attendais pas à te voir.
examples.trans: I wasn't expecting to see you.

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

meanings.note: Je ne sais pas = I don't know. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.
+ infinitive: savoir monter. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.

examples.trans: Do you know where he is?

meanings.note: On your own, without help. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to manage'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'se débrouillé').
débrouille-toi! = sort it out yourself!

examples.text: Il se débrouille bien en français.
examples.trans: He gets by well in French.

examples.text: Alors je me débrouille seule, comme toujours!
examples.trans: So I'll manage on my own, as always!

meanings.note: After the verb. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'alone'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Before the noun: le seul agent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'alone'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Alors je me débrouille seule, comme toujours!
examples.trans: So I'll manage on my own, as always!

meanings.note: Si tu veux = if you want. French conjunction meaning 'if', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
answering a negative question: Aucune nouvelle? - Si!

examples.text: Si tu veux, on peut en parler demain matin.
examples.trans: If you want, we can talk about it tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Dis-moi tout de suite si le rôle t'intéresse.
examples.trans: Tell me right away if the role interests you.

meanings.note: Informal, does not change. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'great'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce serait super si vous pouviez venir.
examples.trans: It would be great if you could come.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé un travail. Super, non?
examples.trans: I found a job. Great, isn't it?

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne sais pas. Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I don't know. I wanted to surprise you.

meanings.note: toujours aucune nouvelle? = still no news?
Invariable French adverb meaning 'always'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse. J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm serious. I've always loved films.

meanings.note: Un travail = a job. Masculine noun ('le travail', plural 'les travaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'work'.

meanings.en: au travail! = let's get to work!
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le travail', plural 'les travaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'work'.

examples.trans: He has a lot of work.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to find'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'trouvé').

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: I don't know. Think of something.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'very'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la vie', plural 'les vies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'life'.

examples.text: Parce que tu ne peux pas. C'est ma vie!
examples.trans: Because you can't. It's my life!

meanings.note: n'avoir rien à voir avec = to have nothing to do with
Voir quelqu'un. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to see'.

examples.text: Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.
Imparfait, softer. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.

examples.trans: I just want to see Mathias.

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: One person, formal. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Several people. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
No preposition. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to listen'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'écouté').

meanings.en: écoute = listen, look (to start a point)
meanings.note: Casual imperative. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to listen'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'écouté').

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.note: The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
